title: test-0000-GEN-AIRQUALITY
passage: Air quality is a complex issue that affects our health daily. Many people mistakenly believe that if the air looks clear and has no smell, it is safe to breathe, but invisible pollutants like PM2.5 are often present. PM2.5 refers to fine particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers or less, which is significantly smaller than PM10 particles. Because of their tiny size, PM2.5 particles are more dangerous as they can penetrate deep into the lungs and bloodstream. Furthermore, air quality is not uniform; a city does not have one fixed AQI that stays the same all day and everywhere in it. Local traffic, industrial activity, and weather patterns cause AQI levels to fluctuate significantly across different neighborhoods and hours. Finally, while indoor plants are beneficial, planting a few trees or keeping a few indoor plants will not fully clean polluted city air. Effective protection requires reducing pollution at the source and using proper equipment like N95 masks, as a cloth mask or a surgical mask does not protect as well as an N95 against PM2.5. Relying on simple visual checks or inadequate filtration leaves individuals exposed to harmful pollutants that remain suspended in the air long after the visible haze clears.
summary: Many people think that if the air is clear and doesn’t have a smell, it’s safe to breathe. But there are also invisible pollutants like PM2.5 in the air. Finally, while indoor plants help clean the air, planting a few trees and keeping a few indoor plants won't make the city clean.
